body.en: A deque (pronounced deck), or double-ended queue, is an ordered linear list in which elements can be inserted and deleted at either end, FRONT or REAR. If insertion and deletion are done at the same end it behaves like a stack; if they are done at opposite ends it behaves like a queue. Applications include re-joining a queue at the front, vehicles moving to the rear of another lane at a toll booth, keeping a browser history or undo list of limited size, and checking whether a string is a palindrome.

title.en: On the board: A deque: insert and delete at both ends

say.en: A deque, or double-ended queue, allows insertion and deletion at both the FRONT and the REAR.
Inserting and deleting at the same end makes it behave like a stack. Opposite ends make it a queue.
With a list: insertFront is insert at 0, insertRear is append, deletionFront is pop of 0, deletionRear is pop.
To test a palindrome, put the letters in a deque and remove one from each end; they must match every time.

narration.en: We draw a deque with operations at both ends, use it as a stack or a queue, and check a palindrome with it.

body.en: With a list myDeque: insertFront uses myDeque.insert(0, element); insertRear uses append(element); deletionFront uses pop(0); deletionRear uses pop(). getFront returns myDeque[0] and getRear returns myDeque[len(myDeque) − 1]. Each deletion must first check that the deque is not empty.

problem.en: Check whether a word is a palindrome using a deque. Give the exact output.

answer.en:
MALAYALAM True
KANNADA False
NOON True

narration.en: Insert every letter at the rear, then remove one from each end and compare. Any mismatch means it is not a palindrome.

body.en: Front means index 0: insert(0, x) and pop(0). Rear means the end of the list: append(x) and pop(). Stack = one end; queue = both ends used separately.

narration.en: Which end, which method?. Front means index 0: insert(0, x) and pop(0). Rear means the end of the list: append(x) and pop(). Stack = one end; queue = both ends used separately.
